headline: Sengun and Houston end Boston's five-game streak

off.text: Next: Wed, Nov 4 vs Bucks, 7:30 PM
Next: Thu, Nov 5 at Penguins, 7:00 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 8 vs Packers, 4:25 PM

storylines: Boston comes home after Monday's 109–93 loss in Houston ended its five-game win streak.
Milwaukee is 1–6, and the teams meet again Sunday in Milwaukee.
Mitchell Robinson sprained his left thumb Monday but returned, and Payton Pritchard has missed 15 straight threes.
celtics.edge: Boston, clearly: it's 5–2 and at home against a 1–6 Bucks team.

storylines: Boston has won two straight and sits second in the East with 23 points.
Matthew Poitras's status is unclear after Monday's elbow to the face.
Pittsburgh is 5–7–2; Evgeni Malkin and Kaedan Korczak are day-to-day, and the Penguins host Vegas on Tuesday.
bruins.edge: Boston: it has 23 points to Pittsburgh's 12, and the Penguins are dealing with injuries.

storylines: Vrabel had no expectations yet on Hunter Henry (foot); Mack Hollins and Reggie Gilliam could return this week.
A.J. Brown (knee) missed the Miami game, and his availability for Green Bay is still unclear.
It's Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame weekend, with the induction Saturday at Patriot Place.
patriots.edge: Even on paper: both teams are 5–3.

results.headline: Sengun and Houston end Boston's five-game streak
results.takeaway: Houston never trailed, and Alperen Sengun went 12-of-15 for 26 points as the Rockets beat a Celtics team resting Paul George on the second night of a back-to-back. Boston shot 12-of-42 from three, and its five-game win streak is over.

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: An even opening quarter. Tari Eason hit two early threes off the Houston bench, and Luka Garza answered with threes of his own as the backup center.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: Houston won the quarter 28–21. Sengun had 12 first-half points on 6-of-8 shooting, and Mitchell Robinson briefly left with a sprained left thumb before returning. Boston closed the half on an 8–4 run capped by a Jayson Tatum three; Tatum had 11 points on 3-of-9 at the break.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Robinson replaced Hugo González in the starting lineup for the second half, and Neemias Queta scored Boston's first 7 points of the quarter. Tatum then picked up two quick offensive fouls, both on charges drawn by Marcus Smart, and sat late in the quarter with four fouls as Boston went 6:17 without a field goal.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Houston pulled away, with Smart hitting two late threes and Reed Sheppard scoring 8 in the quarter. Boston trailed by as many as 18, its largest deficit of the season, and was down 15 when Tatum checked out with 2:29 left. The Rockets outscored Boston 50–34 in the paint and 18–2 on fast breaks.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: Scored or assisted on 43% of Boston's baskets, but had five turnovers and spent part of the third in foul trouble.

performers.name: Neemias Queta
performers.note: Opened the second half with Boston's first 7 points to keep it within reach.

performers.name: Luka Garza
performers.note: He and Baylor Scheierman went 7-of-13 from three; the rest of the team went 5-of-29.

results.oppLine: Alperen Sengun had 26 points on 12-of-15 shooting, 10 assists and 7 rebounds; Jabari Smith Jr. and Amen Thompson scored 14 each, and Kevin Durant had 12 on 5-of-6.

results.headline: Pastrnak's shootout winner holds off Vegas
results.takeaway: David Pastrnak scored the only goal of the shootout after Vegas came back from 2–0 down, and Jeremy Swayman stopped all three Golden Knights shooters. Boston has won six straight at home and sits second in the East with 23 points.

sections.label: 1st period
sections.text: At 7:23, seconds after Carter Hart stopped Nikita Zadorov in the slot, Elias Lindholm collected the puck behind the net and fed James Hagens for his sixth goal, the most among NHL rookies. Boston has scored first in six of its last seven games.

sections.label: 2nd period
sections.text: Braeden Bowman got a five-minute major and a game misconduct at 2:49 for an elbow to Matthew Poitras's face, and Morgan Geekie scored 33 seconds into the major, from Pavel Zacha and Pastrnak, to end Boston's 0-for-10 power-play skid. Poitras returned to the bench but never took another shift. Mark Stone cut it to 2–1 on a power play at 14:58, putting in the rebound of a Tomas Hertl shot; Charlie McAvoy, who took three penalties, was also called for arguing with the officials after the goal.

sections.label: 3rd period
sections.text: Trevor Connelly tied it at 7:23, banking Noah Hanifin's feed from behind the net off Swayman.

sections.label: Overtime
sections.text: No goals in overtime, sending Boston to its first shootout of the season.

sections.label: Shootout
sections.text: Swayman stopped Connelly, Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner, and Pastrnak beat Hart in the third round for the only goal.

performers.name: David Pastrnak
performers.note: Led all skaters with seven shots, set up Geekie's power-play goal and scored the only shootout goal.

performers.name: Jeremy Swayman
performers.note: Gave up two goals in a lead Boston let slip, then stopped all three Vegas shooters.

performers.name: James Hagens
performers.note: His sixth goal leads NHL rookies, and he turns 20 today.

results.oppLine: Mitch Marner had two assists, extending his point streak to 10 games; Mark Stone and Trevor Connelly scored, and Carter Hart made 25 saves.

celtics.headline: Robinson sprains left thumb in Houston
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson briefly left Monday's game with a sprained left thumb and returned with his hand strapped. He finished with 4 points and 4 rebounds in 15:13, a minus-16. "I just haven't found my rhythm yet," he said.

celtics.headline: Tatum named East Player of the Week
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum won his 14th career Eastern Conference Player of the Week award after averaging 30.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 7 assists in a 4-0 week, including a career-high 22 free-throw attempts and a buzzer-beater against Brooklyn.

celtics.headline: George rested on back-to-back
celtics.summary: Paul George, 36, sat out Monday's game in Houston for rest after playing both games of the previous back-to-back. He is Boston's second-leading scorer at 20.7 points a game and is shooting 38.8% from three.

celtics.headline: Pritchard has missed 15 straight threes
celtics.summary: Payton Pritchard went 0-of-5 from three in Houston after 0-of-7 in Orlando, 15 straight misses dating to Friday. Outside his 7-of-10 night against Chicago, he is 6-of-32 from deep this season.

celtics.headline: Tatum on Durant: he 'changed the narrative'
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum said watching Kevin Durant come back from his torn Achilles gave him hope during his own rehab. "He's not the average basketball player," Tatum said of Durant, who has played 75, 62 and 78 games the last three seasons.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla on Cenac: 'I trust him'
celtics.summary: Rookie Chris Cenac Jr., 19, has played seven minutes over two games. "I trust him, I don't know how it's going to go but I trust him," Joe Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Garza backs up, Cenac moves up to third center
celtics.summary: With Robinson resting, Luka Garza played backup center for the first time this season and had 12 points in 21 minutes. Rookie Chris Cenac, 19, moved up to third center.

celtics.headline: Celtics share NBA Cup Group C lead
celtics.summary: Friday's win put Boston at 1-0 in Group C alongside Washington, which beat Charlotte 95-79 earlier in the night; the Wizards lead the point-differential tiebreaker, +16 to +14. Each team plays its four group opponents once, the three East group winners and two wild cards advance, and the knockout rounds begin Dec. 4.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla steers Brown question toward this roster
celtics.summary: On his weekly 98.5 The Sports Hub appearance, Joe Mazzulla declined to engage with a caller's question about Jaylen Brown calling 2025-26 his favorite season. He said players should be able to speak honestly and emphasized trust in the locker room and the 2026-27 group.

bruins.headline: Poitras hurt by Bowman elbow
bruins.summary: Matthew Poitras left Monday's game bleeding after an elbow to the face from Vegas's Braeden Bowman, who got a major and a game misconduct. Poitras returned to the bench but didn't take another shift, and Marco Sturm had no update; his status for Thursday in Pittsburgh is unclear.

bruins.headline: Hagens leads NHL rookies in goals and points
bruins.summary: James Hagens, who turns 20 Tuesday, leads all rookies with six goals and 12 points. His line with Casey Mittelstadt and Elias Lindholm has outscored opponents 7-2 in 113 minutes at 5-on-5.

bruins.headline: Sturm on McAvoy penalties: 'He needs to control' it
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy took three penalties Monday, including a call for arguing with officials after Vegas's power-play goal. "That's something he needs to control, right?" Sturm said.

bruins.headline: Geekie scores in back-to-back games
bruins.summary: Morgan Geekie, who had one goal in his first 14 games, has scored in two straight. His power-play goal Monday ended Boston's 0-for-10 skid with the man advantage.

bruins.headline: Six straight home wins
bruins.summary: Monday's shootout win, Boston's first shootout of the season, was its sixth straight at TD Garden. The Bruins practice in Brighton Tuesday and Wednesday before Thursday's game at Pittsburgh.

bruins.headline: Pastrnak passes Bergeron for third on Bruins' goals list
bruins.summary: David Pastrnak's first-period breakaway goal Saturday was his 428th, moving him past former linemate Patrice Bergeron for third in franchise history. "That is a huge milestone and doing that with one franchise, especially with the Boston Bruins, is pretty amazing," Marco Sturm said.

bruins.headline: 17 Bruins have scored; goalie duo fourth in GAA
bruins.summary: Seventeen Bruins have scored this season and five have at least five goals. Jeremy Swayman and Michael DiPietro rank fourth in the league with a combined 2.33 goals-against average.

bruins.headline: DiPietro makes 37 saves for third NHL win
bruins.summary: Michael DiPietro started Saturday's matinee and stopped 37 of 41 shots, including three in overtime. "It was definitely a crazy third and it just shows you the character of the group," he said.

bruins.headline: 12 of the next 14 on home ice
bruins.summary: After going without a point on the two-game trip to Carolina and St. Louis, the Bruins play 12 of their next 14 games at TD Garden. Boston struck first in both road games but was shut out over the final 50-plus minutes of each.

bruins.headline: McAvoy leads Bruins defensemen in scoring
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy, back from a six-game suspension, leads Boston defensemen with six points (1 goal, 5 assists) in seven games while averaging 25:00 of ice time. He and Hampus Lindholm form the top pair and anchor the first power-play unit.

patriots.headline: Vrabel: no expectations yet on Henry
patriots.summary: Mike Vrabel said Monday he doesn't "have any expectations yet" for Hunter Henry, who left Sunday's game with a foot injury. Mack Hollins and Reggie Gilliam could return this week as they work through the return-to-play process.

patriots.headline: A.J. Brown's availability unclear for Packers
patriots.summary: A.J. Brown missed Sunday's game with a knee injury after being limited earlier in the week by an ankle injury, and didn't travel to Miami. "We'll see where A.J.'s availability is this week," Vrabel said on WEEI.

patriots.headline: Henry, Jacas hurt in Miami
patriots.summary: Hunter Henry (foot) left in the second quarter and was ruled out after briefly returning to the sideline, and rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas (knee) went down in the second half after 1.5 sacks. Updates on both are expected at Wednesday's practice.

patriots.headline: Edge depth thins with Jones also hurt
patriots.summary: Dre'Mont Jones also went down Sunday, leaving Elijah Ponder as the only healthy player the Patriots list at outside linebacker. "It's always tough losing Hunt," Drake Maye said of Henry, adding that he "seems fine in here."

patriots.headline: Trade deadline is Nov. 10
patriots.summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. Asked about trade talks, Vrabel said there are "lots of conversations" and "we'll try to do what we can to make the team better."

patriots.headline: Vrabel backs Borregales after another miss
patriots.summary: After Andy Borregales's third miss from 40 yards or less this season, Vrabel said "I've got a lot of confidence in Andy" but added, "We have to make our kicks."

patriots.headline: Maye's three-TD streak reaches five games
patriots.summary: Drake Maye went 16-of-20 for 199 yards with two touchdown passes and a rushing score, his fifth straight game with at least three total touchdowns. All three came after halftime. "You wanna be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there's not a whole lot of excuses," Mike Vrabel said.

patriots.headline: Season-high five sacks, Byard's first Patriots pick
patriots.summary: New England sacked Malik Willis five times, its most this season, led by Cory Durden and Gabe Jacas with 1.5 each. Kevin Byard's interception, his first as a Patriot, set up the clinching touchdown, and Miami ran for 74 yards.

patriots.headline: Ben Brown takes over at left guard
patriots.summary: Ben Brown replaced Walter Rouse at left guard at halftime in Miami, and pass protection improved after the switch. Carlton Davis III returned after missing three games.

patriots.headline: Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction set for Nov 7
patriots.summary: Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday, Nov. 7 at 1 PM at Patriot Place Plaza. The ceremony is free and open to the public and will stream on Patriots.com. Gronkowski played nine seasons in New England (2010–18) and won three Super Bowls.

redsox.headline: Red Sox designate Zack Kelly, Eduardo Rivera
redsox.summary: Boston designated right-hander Zack Kelly and left-hander Eduardo Rivera for assignment Monday to meet the deadline for reinstating players from the 60-day IL. Kelly, 31, has a 4.04 ERA in 115 games over five seasons; Rivera, 23, had a 2.96 ERA at Triple-A Worcester. The club has seven days to trade, release or waive them.

redsox.headline: No qualifying offers from Boston
redsox.summary: The Red Sox issued no qualifying offers before Monday's deadline. Sonny Gray was ineligible because he had rejected one with the Twins in 2023. Rule 5 protection decisions are due Nov. 17 and non-tenders Nov. 20.

redsox.headline: Red Sox exercise Whitlock's $8.25 million option
redsox.summary: Boston picked up Garrett Whitlock's 2027 club option instead of a $1 million buyout. He had a 1.72 ERA in 54 appearances with 26 holds and pitched through a fractured tibia over the final month; no surgery was needed and he's expected to be ready for spring training.

redsox.headline: Sonny Gray headed to free agency
redsox.summary: Sonny Gray's mutual option for 2027 was declined, triggering a $10 million buyout instead of the $30 million option, and sending the 36-year-old right-hander toward free agency. He posted a 2.72 ERA in 29 starts for Boston this season; the Red Sox can negotiate exclusively with him until Monday.

redsox.headline: Contreras: 'We need some more offense'
redsox.summary: Willson Contreras told the Boston Globe the Red Sox need more offense and that "that's for [Craig] Breslow to figure out." Boston ranked 26th in home runs and 23rd in runs this season; Contreras led the club with 27 homers, 81 RBIs and a .902 OPS.

redsox.headline: Halligan, Bastardo sign minor league deals
redsox.summary: Right-handers Patrick Halligan and Angel Bastardo signed minor league contracts for 2027. Bastardo had a 4.64 ERA with 73 strikeouts in 40 relief appearances at Worcester and is Rule 5-eligible in December.

redsox.headline: Red Sox trade Tsung-Che Cheng to Tigers
redsox.summary: Boston traded infielder Tsung-Che Cheng, 25, to Detroit, a day after dealing Nate Eaton to the A's, as it keeps clearing 40-man roster space. Cheng hit .256 (10-for-37) in 14 games for Boston this season, making 13 starts at shortstop, and .241 with eight homers in 94 games at Triple-A Worcester.

redsox.headline: Red Sox trade Nate Eaton to A's
redsox.summary: Boston's first move of the offseason sent outfielder Nate Eaton to the Athletics for 18-year-old right-hander Jareth Rayo, who had a 5.50 ERA over 36 innings in the Dominican Summer League. Eaton, out of minor league options, hit .244 with two homers and 11 steals in 65 games for Boston over two seasons.

redsox.headline: Red Sox hire Astros' Jason Bell as outfield instructor
redsox.summary: Boston is adding Jason Bell, who spent the past decade with Houston, to its major league staff, including as outfield instructor, per a league source. He was the Astros' field coordinator for two years and quality control coach for one. The Red Sox still have at least two openings under Chad Tracy: first base and third base coach.
